newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST-Lira over 1,000/mark but in ERM bands.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Lira over 1,000/mark but in ERM bands.

text.p: The Italian lira will weaken past 1,000 per mark in coming months but stay within 2.25 percent of its central parity in Europe's currency grid and gravitate back to its 990 per mark anchor by the end of 1997, analysts said.

Reuters collected quarterly forecasts from 15 economists April 1 to 3. Analysts on average saw the lira weakening to 1,005 per mark in the third quarter before turning back towards its central rate in the exchange rate mechanism (ERM) of 990 per mark by the year end.
The Bank of Italy's indicative rate on Wednesday stood at 986.16 lire per mark.
Analysts said mean mark/lira rates were on the whole "reassuring" but there was little consensus on future direction.

With debate over Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) dragging on some foreign banks saw rough times ahead taking the lira past 1,012 per mark, which is 2.25 percent from its central parity and regarded as an unofficial parameter for fluctuation.
"Currency markets will be pushed and pulled one way and another until there is a political decision on Italy's and Spain's entry in EMU," Ottavio Ricchi, economist at DRI-McGraw Hill in Milan said.

Giovanni Polastri analyst at 4CAST in London said: "The lira benefited from a new bout of optimism on EMU after the Noordwijk Ecofin (meeting earlier in April). The convergence process can continue and the market has renewed hopes for an official Italian interest rate cut."
Economists see the Bank of Italy reducing key rates as early as the end of April when consumer price inflation could fall below 2.0 percent. Its discount rate stands at 6.75 percent.
However analysts said the lira's performance will also depend on the direction of U.S. and European interest rates.

"At the end of the third quarter the picture will change - U.S. interest rates will continue to rise and this will revive expectations for a tightening in Germany with negative impact on the lira," Polastri said.
Analysts said in the fourth quarter Italy's future role in Europe will become clearer and lira levels will start discounting the most probable EMU scenario.

"Italy will enter EMU with a one year delay but within a predefined framework. The markets won't mind this. Italy has made a lot of progress in tidying up its finances but needs stability," said Renzo Avesani, economist at Cariplo in Milan.
Avesani saw the lira steady in a 995-990 per mark range, also thanks to positive Italian economic fundamentals.

Marco Ricci, analyst at Centrosim in Milan, saw Italy as one of the founding members of the new single currency and this, along with the firming dollar, explained his forecast also for a lira stable in a 995-990 trading range.
But DRI, which does not see Italy in the first EMU wave, saw the lira weakening to 1,042 per mark in the first quarter 1998.

Analysts' forecasts for the dollar/lira rate indicate a slight appreciation of the Italian currency, firming from 1,700 in the second quarter to 1,650 in the fourth quarter and 1,630 in the first three months of 1998.
On Wednesday the Bank of Italy's indicative rate was at 1,694.42 per dollar when the dollar was at 1.7172 marks.

"The dollar is overvalued against the mark because of the differential between U.S. and German interest rates. This spread will narrow as the economic recovery in Europe picks up. A further Federal Reserve tightening is already priced in," Polastri said.
Avesani said dollar/mark will stabilize between 1.65 and 1.71 marks which will in turn help dollar/lira stay under 1,700 which is considered a point of equilibrium.
